item.text:
<linkedin_post>Transcription speed depends heavily on how the work is measured. NVIDIA reports that Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe processed 100 hours of audio in under three minutes on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPU. That result used a forthcoming quantized version, 30-second clips and high concurrency.

The figure is useful for teams processing large backlogs of recordings, though it doesn’t describe how quickly a single long recording will be ready. Workloads with different clip lengths, hardware or concurrency may perform differently.

The model supports word-level timestamps, which Agora used in a classroom demo to show transcript text alongside a recording. Students can see when something was said during the replay. For that kind of application, speed matters alongside the accuracy of the words and timestamps.</linkedin_post>
